Hi Sara —

Hope you're well. Your renewal is coming up in Jan; pricing in the market has moved and I wanted to propose a structure that locks current rates while giving Velox flexibility on cashflow. Two quick, pragmatic options:

- 24-month prepay: single upfront payment that locks pricing for 24 months; we'd offer a 12% term discount and a staged credit release across the first 6 months to smooth consumption.
- Annualized deposit (preferred practical alternative): Velox prepays 12 months of committed capacity but we amortize the cash impact by allowing an upfront deposit equal to 50% of year one, with the remainder applied in quarterly scheduled credits over Q1–Q2. Pricing would be held flat for the 12-month period and we can add a modest 6% discount vs month-to-month list.

Attached is an initial term sheet with numbers and examples. If procurement needs this to be PSU/PO-friendly we can convert the financial terms into an SOW/PO schedule. Would love to sync on which approach maps best to Velox's finance runway.

Can you share whether Velox prefers CAPEX (large upfront) vs OPEX (spread) so we can tailor?

Sara —

Thanks for the candid constraints. Grace and I talked about two customer-aligned structures that meet Velox's cashflow needs while protecting price:

Option A — 24-month term prepay (best unit economics):
  • 12% off list vs month-to-month
  • Single upfront payment (full prepay)
  • We release usage credits across months 0–6 to ease consumption accounting
  • Good if Velox can treat as CAPEX and wants the strongest discount

Option B — Annualized deposit with amortized upfront (recommended for cashflow):
  • Committed 12-month baseline; pricing hold for 12 months
  • Upfront deposit = 50% of year one (we can take to 40% as Sara asked)
  • Remaining 50% converted into fixed quarterly credits applied to invoices in Q1 and Q2 (schedule enclosed)
  • 6% discount applied to the committed baseline vs month-to-month
  • Overage outside the committed baseline billed at standard rates with a 10% buffer allowance in month-to-month billing before overage kicks in

Attached: Redwood_MultiYear_Term_Sheet_v3.pdf with illustrative cashflow tables and examples for both options.

Questions for you, Sara:
- Would Velox accept 40% upfront (collected at signature) + 60% in credits over first two quarters?
- Do you want the overage buffer to be a % of committed baseline (we typically do 10–15%) or a fixed number of tokens/hours?

If you confirm direction we’ll have Laura/Finance produce a final SOW and an invoice schedule that procurement can attach to the PO.

Thanks —
